mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which can stimulate economic growth and lead to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not higher than baseline during periods of low FEDFUNDS (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rise in unemployment rate above 6.5% signals labor market weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX returns remain positive when UNRATE exceeds 6.5% in >40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Strong GDP growth coupled with increasing employment suggests robust demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Correlation between GDPC1 and PAYEMS with SPX returns is not significant (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: Rising inflation (CPI) in a late-cycle expansion may lead to monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases by 0.5% in a month
failure_condition: SPX returns remain positive despite CPI increase in >50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing housing starts indicate strong demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: 5-day returns are not higher during periods of rising HOUST (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production signals supply chain issues, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX returns remain positive when INDPRO is below 100 in >40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Rising inflation with high federal funds rate indicates tight monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX returns are positive in >30% of cases despite the trigger.

mechanism_narrative: Low unemployment in early expansion signals strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: 5-day returns are not higher when UNRATE is below 5% (t-test p > 0.05).
